clue.text: One of a worldly couple

parts.note: the globe of the world is split into a northern and southern pair of halves, and this is one of that pair

explanation.surface: Someone describes one partner in a sophisticated, worldly married couple.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth is divided into two halves, each one a half of the globe.

clue.text: Transport to Crete? Bully for her!

definitions.text: Transport to Crete? Bully for her!

parts.words: Transport to Crete? Bully for her!
parts.note: in Greek myth Zeus took the form of a bull and carried a princess off to Crete

explanation.surface: Someone cheers a woman who has got herself a passage to Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully for her' is a cheer, but also says a bull was used for her.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Phoenician princess was carried by Zeus in bull form to Crete.

clue.text: Complaint one is always conscious of?

definitions.text: Complaint one is always conscious of?

parts.words: Complaint one is always conscious of?
parts.note: the ailment keeps a sufferer conscious, that is awake, all night

explanation.surface: Someone describes a nagging ailment that never leaves their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic sleeplessness is an ailment that keeps one awake.

clue.text: Before the agitation, promotion

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a ferment is a state of agitation or unrest

explanation.surface: A promotion was granted ahead of the turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement to a higher position is a promotion.

clue.text: Give the palm to the muse of music

explanation.surface: Someone awards the prize to the Greek muse of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give the palm' suggests awarding a prize, but Euterpe is also a genus of palm trees; 'Give' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of tropical palm trees shares its name with the Greek muse who presides over music and lyric poetry.

clue.text: Hill 'of battle

parts.note: the word wanted is the one that goes before Hill to name an English Civil War battle of 1642

explanation.surface: A hill is named for a battle fought on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill, in Warwickshire, was the first big battle of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Put before hill, it names a ridge where a famous 1642 battle took place.

clue.text: This nag's in battle array

indicators.note: battle array puns on arranging, so these letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the letters of the words as written, including the S

explanation.surface: An old horse is drawn up in battle formation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Hastings, 1066, is when the Normans conquered England.
explanation.definitionFit: The decisive 1066 battle in which William of Normandy defeated Harold.

clue.text: What made Lot a widower

parts.note: in Genesis, Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and was turned into a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: Someone asks what cost Lot his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A look back, the glance behind that turned Lot's wife to salt.

clue.text: Be back in time for the discussion

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, so the reversed letters sit within the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word Be the other way round

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone is told to return promptly for a meeting or talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BE into EB, and 'in' puts that inside DATE, giving DEBATE; the printed solution's R is a misprint for B.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument or exchange of views is a discussion.

clue.text: Half Moon Street?.Not yet

explanation.surface: Someone names Half Moon Street, a London address, and admits they have not got there yet.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the shape of a half moon, a curved street, and the old sense 'growing', as the moon is before it is full.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved moon shape, a curved row of houses, and the Latin sense 'increasing', the moon not yet full, all share the word.

clue.text: The location of an uprising

parts.note: an uprising here is literally going up, as in a building's lift, not a rebellion

explanation.surface: A historian asks where a rebellion broke out.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift is the place where people rise from floor to floor.

clue.text: (Hand across) the sea

explanation.surface: A stage direction for a hand stretched over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Across the Channel, in French, 'main' is hand; the Spanish Main is an old name for the sea of the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for hand, and a poetic word for the open ocean.

clue.text: One bringing light into the life of Benedick ?'

definitions.text: One bringing light into the life of Benedick ?'

parts.words: One bringing light into the life of Benedick ?'
parts.note: in Much Ado About Nothing, Benedick is tricked into love with Beatrice; light also suggests someone who makes things that strike fire

explanation.surface: Someone describes who brightened Benedick's life in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Pedro schemes to pair Benedick with Beatrice; someone who makes matches literally brings light.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who arranges romances, or one who makes small sticks for lighting fires.

clue.text: Leading ballerina in tears from-rebukes

indicators.note: the ballerina is placed inside the word for tears

parts.note: rends means tears apart
the prima ballerina is the leading dancer of a company

explanation.surface: A principal dancer weeps after being scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' means rips, not weeping: RENDS, with PRIMA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp scoldings or reproofs are rebukes, as a verb or a noun.

clue.text: Source of superficial sweetness

parts.note: superficial is taken literally as on the surface, the sweet coating spread over a cake

explanation.surface: Someone describes where false charm comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine powdered sugar is used for the sweet top layer on cakes.

clue.text: Sad rite engendering strings of invective

indicators.note: engendering means producing something new, so these letters are rebuilt into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A gloomy ceremony provokes outbursts of angry abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches of abuse are strings of invective.

clue.text: " Sounders " of aggressive horns

parts.note: the horns are car horns, sounded by bullying drivers, not the horns of animals

explanation.surface: Something sounds out the bellow of aggressive horned beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsiderate, bullying motorists who blast their car horns.

clue.text: A tricky way to play

parts.note: in bridge, a tricky way to win a trick is to play a lower card hoping the higher one is held on your right

explanation.surface: Someone describes a crafty way to play a game.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, playing a lower card in hope of a trick is a subtle, skilful manoeuvre.

clue.text: Trade associated with bills in the money market

definitions.text: associated with bills in the money market

explanation.surface: A business deals in bills on the money market.
explanation.walkthrough: A bill of exchange is a written order to pay money, traded in the money market.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade means swapping goods, and bills of exchange are payment orders traded in finance.

clue.text: Establishment with a record turnover ?

parts.note: it looks like a shop selling hit records, but pop is old slang for pawn, so goods are turned over for cash

explanation.surface: Someone praises a business that has had record sales.
explanation.walkthrough: POP SHOP is old British slang for a pawnshop ('pop goes the weasel').
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a pawnbroker's, where possessions are pawned for cash.

clue.text: Gets no hard correction for being wilful

indicators.note: a correction puts things right, so these letters are reordered into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone escapes harsh punishment for being stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person who insists on their own way is wilful.

clue.text: Christian in Egypt caught the sound of this

indicators.note: we want a word that is spoken like the word for caught

parts.note: copped is slang for caught

explanation.surface: A Christian in Egypt overheard something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' is COPPED, which is said like COPT; 'this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Copts are the native Christian church of Egypt.

clue.text: Macbeth, wanted it to go, to the dogs'

definitions.text: Macbeth, wanted it to go, to the dogs'

parts.words: Macbeth, wanted it to go, to the dogs'
parts.note: I'll none of it' when the doctor cannot cure his wife

explanation.surface: Macbeth wished something would go to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Old word for medicine, which Macbeth tells the doctor to throw away.

clue.text: They take collections at smoking concerts

definitions.text: They take collections at smoking concerts

parts.words: They take collections at smoking concerts
parts.note: the collections are not donations but cigarette ends and ash gathered at an informal concert where smoking was allowed

explanation.surface: Volunteers pass round the hat at informal men's concerts where smoking was allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dishes for cigarette ash gather what smokers leave behind.

clue.text: Part of a church in the last stage of collapse

indicators.note: the final four letters of the word collapse give the answer

explanation.surface: A church building is close to falling down.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Address for one of the top people

definitions.text: Address for one of the top people

parts.words: Address for one of the top people
parts.note: address means a form of title, used for a royal person, with a play on top meaning high

explanation.surface: Someone asks where an important person lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal princes and princesses are addressed by this title.

clue.text: Numbers all in a row

explanation.surface: Some figures are lined up neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: Eights are the figure 8, and also rowing crews of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Several of the figure 8, and racing crews of eight oars who all row.

clue.text: Can actors get this in the green room?

definitions.text: Can actors get this in the green room?

parts.words: Can actors get this in the green room?
parts.note: green also means ..., so the question is whether novice actors can learn their craft

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether performers pick anything up while waiting backstage.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge gained through practice is what green novices lack.
